title: One repository, three deployables, one content platform
ariaLabel: Architecture diagram of a multi-brand CMS. A shared package layer containing a design system, CMS blocks and a data layer feeds three per-brand Next.js applications, which all read from a single Payload CMS backed by one PostgreSQL database.
description: Every brand is the same application with different configuration. Adding one is a config entry and a theme, not a fork — which is the only reason the shared layer stays shared over time.
The design system, the CMS block definitions and the data layer are versioned together. A block added once becomes available to every brand in the same release.
One Payload schema with brand-scoped records, on one PostgreSQL instance. Editors work in a single admin rather than three, and a migration runs once.
The outcome that mattered was onboarding cost: standing up a new brand became a day's configuration, and the proportion of code that stayed shared is what kept maintenance flat as brands were added.
